body_en: Police: 110. Fire and ambulance: 119. Both work from any phone.

title_en: No eating or drinking on the MRT
body_en: Past the yellow line at the ticket gates, eating, drinking (even water) and chewing gum are banned and can be fined. Finish your bubble tea before the gate.
The dark blue seats on trains and buses are for the elderly, pregnant passengers and people with disabilities. Many locals leave them empty even when the train is full.
A stored-value card for MRT, buses, YouBike and convenience stores. Buy and top it up at MRT stations or any 7-Eleven / FamilyMart.
7-Eleven and FamilyMart sell hot food and drinks, top up cards, have ATMs, print documents and pay bills. There is one on almost every corner.
Night market stalls, small eateries and traditional shops are often cash only. Cards work in malls, chains and most hotels.
Tipping is not expected. Sit-down restaurants may add a 10% service charge to the bill.

Public trash bins are rare. Keep a small bag for your trash; convenience stores and MRT stations usually have bins. Garbage trucks play classical music (often Für Elise) so residents know to come out.
Locals boil or filter tap water. Many stations, museums and hotels have free filtered water dispensers, so bring a bottle.
Step over the raised door threshold, never on it. Facing the temple, enter through the right-hand (dragon) door and leave through the left-hand (tiger) door. Ask before photographing people praying.
Scooters are everywhere and turning vehicles do not always yield to pedestrians, even on a green light. Look both ways twice. Sidewalks under shop arcades can be uneven.
At MRT platforms people wait in lines marked on the floor beside the doors and let passengers off first.
